slides.title: LIMITING REAGENT PROBLEMS, STEP BY STEP
THE 4-STEP METHOD
lines: 4. The smaller result is the limiting reagent
slides.note: The limiting reagent runs out first and caps the product.

slides.title: EXAMPLE
slides.problem: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O. You have 4.0 mol H₂ and 3.0 mol O₂. Which is limiting?
steps: 2.0 is smaller, so H₂ is limiting

slides.title: THEORETICAL YIELD
slides.problem: How much H₂O forms from the 4.0 mol H₂?
steps: 4.0 mol H₂ × (2 mol H₂O / 2 mol H₂)

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: The reactant with fewer moles is limiting
points: Compare moles divided by coefficient, not raw moles.
Convert grams to moles first. Comparing grams is a common mistake.
